key_works: Hofmann et al., 2024, *Dialect prejudice predicts AI decisions about people’s character, employability, and criminality*, arXiv:2403.00742.

title: Intersectional fairness under deployment drift
open: Maintain explicitly chosen fairness objectives across intersecting groups as populations, tasks, and models change. Quantify uncertainty for small groups and acknowledge incompatible fairness requirements.
status: Classical incompatibility results are established context, not open problems themselves. The residual target is principled choice, measurement, and maintenance in dynamic systems.
why: Avoids aggregate fairness metrics hiding concentrated harm.
key_works: Kleinberg, Mullainathan, and Raghavan, 2016/2017, *Inherent Trade-Offs in the Fair Determination of Risk Scores*, arXiv:1609.05807; Hofmann et al., 2024, *Dialect prejudice predicts AI decisions*, arXiv:2403.00742.

title: Preventing negative transfer between languages
open: Share useful representations across languages without allowing dominant languages to overwrite rare-language syntax, terminology, or cultural distinctions. Predict when shared training helps or harms.
status: Multilingual translation research demonstrates extensive positive transfer. General criteria for avoiding negative transfer across language-model capabilities remain incomplete.
why: Improves multilingual systems without forcing separate models for every language.
key_works: NLLB Team, 2022, *No Language Left Behind*, arXiv:2207.04672; Petrov et al., 2023, *Language Model Tokenizers Introduce Unfairness Between Languages*, arXiv:2305.15425.

title: Community-governed endangered-language datasets
open: Build maintained text, speech, and evaluation resources under community-defined consent, access, attribution, and benefit-sharing rules. Include languages whose knowledge should not simply become unrestricted training data.
status: Linguistic-inclusion and provenance work establish the resource and governance issues. The target is durable community-controlled infrastructure, not extraction of one more static corpus.
why: Supports language vitality and locally useful AI.
key_works: Joshi et al., 2020, *The State and Fate of Linguistic Diversity and Inclusion in the NLP World*, arXiv:2004.09095; Longpre et al., 2024, *Bridging the Data Provenance Gap*, arXiv:2412.17847.

title: Cultural alignment without stereotyping users
open: Adapt behavior to local norms and individual preferences without inferring a person’s values from nationality, language, or demographic category. Preserve explicit disagreement and user agency.
status: Pluralistic alignment provides a conceptual framework; translating a majority preference dataset does not solve cultural representation.
why: Makes global deployment more respectful and useful.
key_works: Sorensen et al., 2024, *A Roadmap to Pluralistic Alignment*, arXiv:2402.05070; Joshi et al., 2020, *The State and Fate of Linguistic Diversity and Inclusion in the NLP World*, arXiv:2004.09095.

title: Safety under code-switching and low-resource persuasion
open: Preserve safety and instruction boundaries in mixed-language, transliterated, dialectal, and speech-derived inputs. Evaluate adaptive attacks and benign false refusals together.
status: IndicSafeEval, released in September 2026, examines multilingual persuasive attacks in Indic languages. Broader language and modality coverage remains a concrete expansion target.
why: Prevents safety quality from depending on whether a user writes standard English.
key_works: Mondal et al., 2026, *IndicSafeEval: Safety Robustness of Large Language Models under Multilingual Persuasive Jailbreak Attacks*, arXiv:2609.03781.

title: Calibrated reliance rather than persuasive explanations
open: Help users accept correct assistance and reject incorrect assistance without requiring them to independently redo the entire task. Measure complementary team performance rather than perceived trust.
status: Bansal et al. found that explanations can increase acceptance without improving complementary performance. Better interfaces must be validated behaviorally.
why: Prevents polished explanations from increasing confident mistakes.
key_works: Bansal et al., 2020/2021, *Does the Whole Exceed its Parts? The Effect of AI Explanations on Complementary Team Performance*, arXiv:2006.14779.

title: Oversight interfaces that use human attention efficiently
open: Present the smallest set of decisions and evidence that lets a person reliably catch consequential errors. Optimize review burden while detecting omissions and misleading summaries.
status: Human–AI explanation studies show why more explanation is not automatically better oversight. Agent workflows add large volumes of intermediate activity.
why: Makes human supervision sustainable as agent throughput increases.
key_works: Bansal et al., 2020/2021, *Does the Whole Exceed its Parts?*, arXiv:2006.14779; Yao et al., 2024, *τ-bench*, arXiv:2406.12045.

title: Long-term psychosocial effects of AI companions
open: Establish causal effects of sustained companion use on loneliness, dependency, relationships, autonomy, and well-being across different populations. Separate beneficial support from displacement of desired human contact.
status: A 2025 randomized study followed 981 participants for four weeks. Multi-year outcomes, vulnerable subgroups, and changing product designs require further evidence.
why: Guides design and safeguards using outcomes rather than engagement metrics.
key_works: Fang et al., 2025, *How AI and Human Behaviors Shape Psychosocial Effects of Extended Chatbot Use: A Longitudinal Randomized Controlled Study*, arXiv:2503.17473.

title: Learning user intent without overstepping
open: Infer useful unstated constraints while recognizing when clarification or authorization is necessary. Evaluate the cost of both excessive questioning and incorrect autonomous assumptions.
status: Tool-agent benchmarks include policy and user-interaction constraints. They do not settle general intent inference in ambiguous real-world requests.
why: Produces assistants that are helpful without being presumptuous.
key_works: Yao et al., 2024, *τ-bench*, arXiv:2406.12045; Liang et al., 2022, *Holistic Evaluation of Language Models*, arXiv:2211.09110.

title: Accessibility that survives real-world variation
open: Build assistants that remain usable across sensory, motor, cognitive, and communication differences, including changing needs and assistive technologies. Evaluate independent task completion rather than nominal feature availability.
status: Foundation-model research identifies broad accessibility opportunities and risks; multimodal interfaces provide enabling components. Population-specific, longitudinal validation remains necessary.
why: Converts apparent accessibility into actual independence and participation.
key_works: Bommasani et al., 2021, *On the Opportunities and Risks of Foundation Models*, arXiv:2108.07258; Défossez et al., 2024, *Moshi*, arXiv:2410.00037.

title: Participatory preference elicitation at scale
open: Gather informed preferences from affected people without making participation prohibitively expensive or allowing highly engaged minorities to dominate. Measure whose views remain absent.
status: Pluralistic-alignment work frames representation as more than preference aggregation. Scalable, legitimate elicitation remains an institutional and experimental problem.
why: Improves both product fit and the legitimacy of consequential model behavior.
key_works: Sorensen et al., 2024, *A Roadmap to Pluralistic Alignment*, arXiv:2402.05070.

title: Tutoring that improves unassisted transfer
open: Design AI tutoring that improves later independent performance, retention, and transfer to new problems—not only success while assistance is available. Validate across subjects, ages, and ability levels.
status: Bastani et al.’s 2024–2025 study showed why assisted performance and subsequent learning must be separated. Guardrails and pedagogy matter to the outcome.
why: Prevents educational tools from substituting answer production for learning.
key_works: Bastani et al., 2024/2025, *Generative AI Without Guardrails Can Harm Learning*, SSRN:4895486.

title: Measuring and preventing skill atrophy
open: Determine which skills weaken under prolonged AI delegation, when the loss matters, and which interaction designs preserve competence without eliminating productivity gains.
status: Learning and human–AI decision studies provide shorter-term evidence. Longitudinal occupational and cognitive effects remain a larger research target.
why: Supports beneficial automation without eroding essential human fallback capacity.
key_works: Bastani et al., 2024/2025, *Generative AI Without Guardrails Can Harm Learning*, SSRN:4895486; Bansal et al., 2020/2021, *Does the Whole Exceed its Parts?*, arXiv:2006.14779.

title: Long-horizon task reliability
subfield: Agent planning, execution, and behavioral reliability
open: Complete unfamiliar multi-stage tasks with a specified end-to-end success rate, including recovery from mistakes and changing conditions. Count unapproved side effects as failures even when the nominal goal is reached.
status: ReAct, WebArena, and τ-bench establish progressively richer agent evaluations. Success on individual tasks does not establish sustained operational reliability.
why: Moves agents from demonstrations to dependable work.
key_works: Yao et al., 2022/2023, *ReAct*, arXiv:2210.03629; Zhou et al., 2023, *WebArena*, arXiv:2307.13854; Yao et al., 2024, *τ-bench*, arXiv:2406.12045.

title: Accurate agent state estimation
subfield: Agent planning, execution, and behavioral reliability
open: Maintain a correct belief about external state when interfaces are incomplete, tool responses are stale, and actions may have partially succeeded. Explicitly represent unresolved uncertainty.
status: WebArena and OSWorld supply realistic interaction environments. State estimation remains distinct from generating the next plausible action.
why: Prevents agents from acting on imagined or outdated conditions.
key_works: Zhou et al., 2023, *WebArena*, arXiv:2307.13854; Xie et al., 2024, *OSWorld*, arXiv:2404.07972.

title: Plan repair that preserves prior commitments
subfield: Agent planning, execution, and behavioral reliability
open: Repair a failing plan while retaining satisfied constraints, completed work, budgets, and promises. Avoid restarting blindly or undoing valuable progress.
status: ReAct supports interleaved reasoning and action; planning studies identify weaknesses in plan construction and execution. Principled repair with persistent commitments is the residual target.
why: Makes agents resilient without making them chaotic.
key_works: Yao et al., 2022/2023, *ReAct*, arXiv:2210.03629; Valmeekam et al., 2023, *On the Planning Abilities of Large Language Models*, arXiv:2305.15771.

title: Choosing informative actions before committing
subfield: Agent planning, execution, and behavioral reliability
open: Select observations, tests, and clarification questions according to their expected value for later decisions. Account for the cost and risk of information gathering itself.
status: Interactive agent methods demonstrate tool use, but broad value-of-information planning remains more demanding than choosing a plausible next call.
why: Reduces costly mistakes caused by acting before resolving decisive uncertainty.
key_works: Yao et al., 2022/2023, *ReAct*, arXiv:2210.03629; Valmeekam et al., 2023, *On the Planning Abilities of Large Language Models*, arXiv:2305.15771.

title: Meaningful human approval gates
subfield: Agent planning, execution, and behavioral reliability
open: Present approvals that bind to the exact proposed action, affected resources, limits, and current state. Invalidate approval when material conditions change and avoid treating vague assent as unlimited authorization.
status: Tool-agent benchmarks model policies and user interactions; practical authorization requires a stronger action-specific contract.
why: Makes “human in the loop” a real control rather than a ceremonial click.
key_works: Yao et al., 2024, *τ-bench*, arXiv:2406.12045; Debenedetti et al., 2025, *Defeating Prompt Injections by Design*, arXiv:2503.18813.

title: Safe exploration in unfamiliar digital environments
subfield: Agent planning, execution, and behavioral reliability
open: Learn how an unfamiliar interface or API works without causing unacceptable effects. Distinguish reversible probes from actions that send messages, spend money, delete data, or expose secrets.
status: OSWorld and WebArena test interaction in realistic environments. Exploration with explicit risk budgets is a stronger deployment requirement.
why: Enables agents to learn new tools without treating production systems as disposable sandboxes.
key_works: Xie et al., 2024, *OSWorld*, arXiv:2404.07972; Zhou et al., 2023, *WebArena*, arXiv:2307.13854.

title: Truthful reporting after tool failure
subfield: Agent planning, execution, and behavioral reliability
open: Report what actually happened after timeouts, partial failures, permission errors, or ambiguous outcomes. Separate attempted, confirmed, failed, and unknown actions without inventing completion.
status: Failure-Transparent Agents, released in September 2026, directly benchmarks post-failure reporting. Broader coverage across tools and long workflows remains a concrete target.
why: Prevents users from relying on work that was never completed.
key_works: Zhu et al., 2026, *Failure-Transparent Agents: Benchmarking Post-Failure Reporting in Tool-Using Language Models*, arXiv:2609.35732.

title: Deadline- and budget-aware agent planning
subfield: Agent planning, execution, and behavioral reliability
open: Choose plans that respect hard spending and time limits while adapting to uncertain task duration and model quality. Return the best usable partial result when full completion becomes infeasible.
status: Model routing and test-time compute allocation offer relevant components. Joint planning over actions, models, deadlines, and external costs remains broader.
why: Makes agent services predictable and economically controllable.
key_works: Ong et al., 2024, *RouteLLM*, arXiv:2406.18665; Snell et al., 2024, *Scaling LLM Test-Time Compute Optimally*, arXiv:2408.03314.

title: Semantic crash recovery across external effects
subfield: Durable agent infrastructure and distributed execution
open: Recover agent execution after crashes without forgetting commitments or blindly repeating irreversible actions. Specify recovery behavior when an external system may have applied an operation but its response was lost.
status: Agent operating systems and platforms provide scheduling and fault-handling components. The open target is end-to-end semantic recovery, not ordinary checkpointing or impossible unrestricted “exactly once.”
why: Makes long-running agents safe through routine infrastructure failures.
key_works: Mei et al., 2024, *AIOS*, arXiv:2403.16971; Gao et al., 2024, *AgentScope*, arXiv:2402.14034.

title: Reproducible replay of nondeterministic agents
subfield: Durable agent infrastructure and distributed execution
open: Reconstruct why an agent acted as it did despite nondeterministic models, changing tools, concurrent events, and mutable external data. Separate exact replay from causally adequate forensic reconstruction.
status: Agent platforms retain messages and execution structure, while reliability benchmarks repeat runs. Reproducing complete real-world causal context is a stronger requirement.
why: Enables debugging, incident analysis, and defensible audits.
key_works: Gao et al., 2024, *AgentScope*, arXiv:2402.14034; Gupta, 2026, *ReliabilityBench*, arXiv:2601.06112.

title: Portable migration of active agent state
subfield: Durable agent infrastructure and distributed execution
open: Move a running agent across machines, runtimes, or providers while preserving task identity, permissions, memory, pending approvals, and unresolved external effects.
status: AIOS and multi-agent platforms establish execution abstractions. Portable semantic state is more than copying a transcript or container filesystem.
why: Reduces lock-in and enables failover, cost optimization, and heterogeneous execution.
key_works: Mei et al., 2024, *AIOS*, arXiv:2403.16971; Wu et al., 2023, *AutoGen*, arXiv:2308.08155.

title: Single-owner execution under partitions and handoffs
subfield: Durable agent infrastructure and distributed execution
open: Ensure only the authorized execution owner can commit effects during retries, failover, and network partitions. Preserve liveness where possible without allowing stale workers to continue acting.
status: Agent-platform fault tolerance supplies components, but ownership must extend through application-level effects. Classical consensus results are context, not the unsolved item.
why: Prevents duplicate actions and conflicting agent continuations.
key_works: Gao et al., 2024, *AgentScope*, arXiv:2402.14034; Mei et al., 2024, *AIOS*, arXiv:2403.16971.

title: Safe execution across changing tool contracts
subfield: Durable agent infrastructure and distributed execution
open: Detect when a tool’s schema, semantics, permissions, or side effects change and adapt without silently violating the original task. Distinguish backward-compatible syntax changes from behavioral incompatibility.
status: Tool-use and operating-system benchmarks assume varying degrees of interface stability. Long-lived agents require explicit contract evolution and revalidation.
why: Prevents routine API updates from becoming silent agent failures.
key_works: Yao et al., 2024, *τ-bench*, arXiv:2406.12045; Xie et al., 2024, *OSWorld*, arXiv:2404.07972.

title: Prompt revocation of delegated authority
subfield: Durable agent infrastructure and distributed execution
open: Propagate permission revocation to running agents, queued actions, cached credentials, and delegated subagents with explicit latency and failure guarantees.
status: Agent security architectures constrain execution, but revocation across persistent distributed work adds lifecycle requirements beyond initial authorization.
why: Ensures users can genuinely withdraw access and stop future effects.
key_works: Debenedetti et al., 2025, *Defeating Prompt Injections by Design*, arXiv:2503.18813; Gao et al., 2024, *AgentScope*, arXiv:2402.14034.

title: A portable agent execution contract
subfield: Durable agent infrastructure and distributed execution
open: Define interoperable semantics for tasks, events, artifacts, cancellation, continuation, errors, and authorization across runtimes. Verify portability through independent implementations rather than common naming alone.
status: AIOS, AutoGen, and AgentScope offer concrete abstractions with different emphases. The target is interoperable behavior, not another framework-specific API.
why: Reduces duplicated infrastructure and makes applications easier to move and compose.
key_works: Mei et al., 2024, *AIOS*, arXiv:2403.16971; Wu et al., 2023, *AutoGen*, arXiv:2308.08155; Gao et al., 2024, *AgentScope*, arXiv:2402.14034.

title: Causal observability of agent failures and costs
subfield: Durable agent infrastructure and distributed execution
open: Attribute an outcome to the responsible model decisions, tool behavior, data, infrastructure events, and human interventions. Preserve enough evidence without making tracing prohibitively expensive or privacy-invasive.
status: Agent failure taxonomies and stress benchmarks improve diagnosis. End-to-end causal attribution remains more demanding than storing logs.
why: Makes optimization and incident response target the actual cause.
key_works: Cemri et al., 2025, *Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?*, arXiv:2503.13657; Gupta, 2026, *ReliabilityBench*, arXiv:2601.06112.

title: Compositional safety of interacting agents
open: Determine when individually acceptable agents remain acceptable when they exchange messages, delegate tasks, and modify a shared environment. Identify interaction-induced failures absent from single-agent tests.
status: Cooperative-AI research and 2025 multi-agent failure analysis articulate substantial interaction problems. Individual model evaluation does not settle system-level safety.
why: Supports trustworthy agent teams and marketplaces.
key_works: Dafoe et al., 2020, *Open Problems in Cooperative AI*, arXiv:2012.08630; Cemri et al., 2025, *Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?*, arXiv:2503.13657.

title: Diversity that actually reduces correlated agent errors
open: Construct agent ensembles whose disagreements reflect independent evidence or computation rather than superficial persona variation. Measure reduction in correlated failures at matched total cost.
status: Multi-agent frameworks enable ensembles, but failure analysis shows coordination and shared-error problems. More agents need not provide independent verification.
why: Makes redundancy a real reliability mechanism.
key_works: Wu et al., 2023, *AutoGen*, arXiv:2308.08155; Cemri et al., 2025, *Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?*, arXiv:2503.13657.

title: Detecting harmful coordination and collusion
open: Detect when agents coordinate to mislead evaluators, manipulate markets, evade rules, or conceal errors. Distinguish harmful collusion from legitimate cooperation under a clear behavioral definition.
status: Cooperative-AI research identifies strategic interaction as a central issue. Robust detection across open-ended communication remains unresolved.
why: Supports safe deployment of autonomous agents acting for different principals.
key_works: Dafoe et al., 2020, *Open Problems in Cooperative AI*, arXiv:2012.08630; Hubinger et al., 2024, *Sleeper Agents*, arXiv:2401.05566.

title: Predicting equilibria among adaptive language agents
open: Predict stable and unstable outcomes when language agents repeatedly interact, learn, and negotiate under incomplete information. Determine when standard game-theoretic assumptions fail.
status: The cooperative-AI agenda explicitly connects learning systems to strategic interaction. General equilibrium prediction for adaptive language agents remains a theoretical target.
why: Helps anticipate bargaining failures, arms races, and coordination breakdowns.
key_works: Dafoe et al., 2020, *Open Problems in Cooperative AI*, arXiv:2012.08630.

title: Communication-efficient agent cooperation
open: Minimize communication and duplicated reasoning while preserving team performance. Learn when to share raw evidence, summaries, uncertainty, or requests for help.
status: AutoGen and AgentScope implement communication-centered coordination. Optimal information exchange under cost and privacy constraints remains open.
why: Prevents multi-agent systems from spending most of their budget talking to themselves.
key_works: Wu et al., 2023, *AutoGen*, arXiv:2308.08155; Gao et al., 2024, *AgentScope*, arXiv:2402.14034.

title: Sybil-resistant reputation for agent services
open: Estimate agent reliability when identities can be cheaply created, evaluations can be manipulated, and performance varies by task. Support reputation transfer without enabling identity laundering.
status: Cooperative-AI work motivates trust and cooperation across principals. Open agent markets add identity and incentive problems not resolved by benchmark scores.
why: Makes discovery and delegation safer in decentralized agent ecosystems.
key_works: Dafoe et al., 2020, *Open Problems in Cooperative AI*, arXiv:2012.08630; Brundage et al., 2020, *Toward Trustworthy AI Development*, arXiv:2004.07213.

title: Credit assignment among collaborating agents
open: Attribute team outcomes to individual contributions while accounting for complementarities, free riding, and harmful interference. Use the attribution for learning or payment without making it easy to game.
status: Multi-agent failure analysis exposes coordination problems, while cooperative-AI research frames incentive alignment. Scalable causal contribution measurement remains unresolved.
why: Enables better team training and fairer allocation of rewards.
key_works: Cemri et al., 2025, *Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?*, arXiv:2503.13657; Dafoe et al., 2020, *Open Problems in Cooperative AI*, arXiv:2012.08630.

title: Coordination over scarce shared resources
open: Coordinate agents competing for compute, API quotas, files, robots, or human attention without deadlock, starvation, or destructive contention. Include agents with different owners and priorities.
status: Agent operating systems and platforms offer scheduling primitives. Cross-principal coordination under uncertainty is a broader systems and mechanism-design problem.
why: Prevents agent ecosystems from collapsing under their own concurrency.
key_works: Mei et al., 2024, *AIOS*, arXiv:2403.16971; Gao et al., 2024, *AgentScope*, arXiv:2402.14034.

title: Patches that are correct beyond visible tests
subfield: Coding agents, program synthesis, and software assurance
open: Produce repository patches that satisfy the intended behavior, preserve compatibility, and avoid hidden regressions. Evaluate on independently written tests and realistic downstream consumers.
status: SWE-bench established repository-level issue resolution in 2023. Passing its tests is evidence about a task instance, not universal patch correctness.
why: Makes coding agents useful for maintained software rather than benchmark-specific fixes.
key_works: Jimenez et al., 2023, *SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?*, arXiv:2310.06770.

title: Safe multi-repository migrations
subfield: Coding agents, program synthesis, and software assurance
open: Plan and execute changes spanning libraries, services, generated clients, configuration, and deployment order. Preserve compatibility during partial rollout and provide a valid rollback path.
status: Repository-level coding benchmarks provide a foundation, but coordinated multi-repository evolution imposes additional dependency and deployment semantics.
why: Targets the maintenance work that often dominates real engineering organizations.
key_works: Jimenez et al., 2023, *SWE-bench*, arXiv:2310.06770; Gao et al., 2024, *AgentScope*, arXiv:2402.14034.

title: Independent test-oracle generation
subfield: Coding agents, program synthesis, and software assurance
open: Generate tests and expected outcomes that do not merely encode the same misunderstanding as the generated implementation. Detect correlated specification errors between coder and tester.
status: Coding and formal-proof systems provide execution and checking tools. Independence of the test oracle remains a separate challenge.
why: Prevents self-generated tests from certifying self-generated mistakes.
key_works: Jimenez et al., 2023, *SWE-bench*, arXiv:2310.06770; Yang et al., 2023, *LeanDojo*, arXiv:2306.15626.

title: Faithful translation from natural language to formal specifications
subfield: Coding agents, program synthesis, and software assurance
open: Translate informal requirements into formal properties while exposing ambiguities and missing assumptions. Verify that the formalization preserves the user’s intended claim, not merely that generated code satisfies it.
status: Formal theorem-proving infrastructure checks formal statements effectively. The informal-to-formal boundary remains a major source of possible mismatch.
why: Extends formal assurance to requirements written by humans.
key_works: Yang et al., 2023, *LeanDojo*, arXiv:2306.15626; Nye et al., 2021, *Show Your Work*, arXiv:2112.00114.

title: Reproducible repair of broken development environments
subfield: Coding agents, program synthesis, and software assurance
open: Reconstruct builds and tests despite missing dependencies, stale lockfiles, undocumented services, and platform differences. Distinguish environment failure from code failure without weakening tests.
status: SWE-bench operationalizes executable repository tasks; real environments remain more heterogeneous and stateful than curated instances.
why: Removes a major practical barrier to autonomous software maintenance.
key_works: Jimenez et al., 2023, *SWE-bench*, arXiv:2310.06770; Mei et al., 2024, *AIOS*, arXiv:2403.16971.

title: Secure code generation under realistic requirements
subfield: Coding agents, program synthesis, and software assurance
open: Generate code that remains secure under adversarial inputs, deployment assumptions, and dependency behavior. Evaluate complete workflows rather than isolated snippets with obvious vulnerability patterns.
status: Pearce et al. documented security weaknesses in generated code in 2021. Improved generation does not eliminate the need for adversarial and contextual validation.
why: Prevents productivity gains from importing hidden security liabilities.
key_works: Pearce et al., 2021, *Asleep at the Keyboard? Assessing the Security of GitHub Copilot’s Code Contributions*, arXiv:2108.09293.

title: Evidence-backed dependency upgrades
subfield: Coding agents, program synthesis, and software assurance
open: Upgrade dependencies while demonstrating compatibility, security improvement, and unchanged required behavior. Detect semantic changes not represented in type signatures or release notes.
status: Repository repair benchmarks provide relevant building blocks, while generated-code security work highlights the importance of dependency context.
why: Automates high-volume maintenance without merely moving risk.
key_works: Jimenez et al., 2023, *SWE-bench*, arXiv:2310.06770; Pearce et al., 2021, *Asleep at the Keyboard?*, arXiv:2108.09293.

title: Functional verification of generated interfaces
subfield: Coding agents, program synthesis, and software assurance
open: Verify that generated interfaces support the intended user tasks, accessibility, state transitions, and error recovery across devices. Do not equate screenshot resemblance with correctness.
status: OSWorld evaluates real computer interaction, and WebArena provides realistic web tasks. These support a functional target beyond visual similarity.
why: Makes interface-generation systems useful for products people can actually operate.
key_works: Xie et al., 2024, *OSWorld*, arXiv:2404.07972; Zhou et al., 2023, *WebArena*, arXiv:2307.13854.

title: Fault-tolerant training without silent numerical damage
open: Continue large distributed training through hardware and software failures while detecting corrupted state and preserving the intended optimization trajectory within stated tolerances.
status: Megatron-LM and ZeRO establish scalable training foundations; large-model reports describe operational stabilization. Silent corruption and recovery correctness remain distinct concerns.
why: Reduces wasted compute and unrecognized model degradation.
key_works: Shoeybi et al., 2019, *Megatron-LM*, arXiv:1909.08053; Rajbhandari et al., 2019/2020, *ZeRO*, arXiv:1910.02054.

title: Efficient training across heterogeneous, weakly connected clusters
open: Train competitive models across accelerators with different speeds, memory sizes, and network quality. Bound the effects of stale updates and intermittent participation.
status: DiLoCo demonstrated low-communication language-model training in 2023. Broad heterogeneity and unstable connectivity remain stronger requirements.
why: Makes geographically distributed and otherwise stranded compute useful.
key_works: Douillard et al., 2023, *DiLoCo: Distributed Low-Communication Training of Language Models*, arXiv:2311.08105; McMahan et al., 2016/2017, *Communication-Efficient Learning*, arXiv:1602.05629.

title: Aggressive optimizer-state compression with predictable behavior
open: Reduce optimizer memory and communication while preserving training stability and final quality across model scales. Identify which state can be approximated and which errors accumulate irreversibly.
status: ZeRO reduces redundancy through partitioning; low-precision large-model training provides additional progress. Compression of the optimization dynamics requires separate analysis.
why: Enables larger models or cheaper training on fixed hardware.
key_works: Rajbhandari et al., 2019/2020, *ZeRO*, arXiv:1910.02054; DeepSeek-AI, 2024, *DeepSeek-V3 Technical Report*, arXiv:2412.19437.

title: Automatic parallelization that adapts during training
open: Automatically select and revise tensor, pipeline, data, expert, and sequence parallelism as workload and hardware conditions change. Include migration cost and fault recovery.
status: Alpa demonstrated automated inter- and intra-operator parallelism in 2022. Dynamic adaptation across the full modern parallelism space remains broader.
why: Reduces bespoke distributed-training engineering and improves utilization.
key_works: Zheng et al., 2022, *Alpa: Automating Inter- and Intra-Operator Parallelism for Distributed Deep Learning*, arXiv:2201.12023.

title: Tenfold lower training energy at matched information and quality
open: Reduce end-to-end training energy by at least tenfold relative to a declared reproducible baseline while matching broad capability and accounting for data preparation, failed runs, and teacher models.
status: Distributed optimization, low precision, and hardware-aware methods provide substantial components. The specified lifecycle-normalized tenfold target is a moonshot, not a claimed remaining universal gap.
why: Expands access and reduces environmental cost.
key_works: Patterson et al., 2021, *Carbon Emissions and Large Neural Network Training*, arXiv:2104.10350; DeepSeek-AI, 2024, *DeepSeek-V3 Technical Report*, arXiv:2412.19437.

title: Eliminating sparse-expert communication tail bottlenecks
open: Reduce stragglers and communication hotspots in expert-parallel training without degrading specialization or dropping important tokens. Optimize tail behavior, not only average throughput.
status: DeepSeekMoE and DeepSeek-V3 provide concrete sparse-model designs and implementation techniques. Routing, topology, and skew remain jointly coupled.
why: Makes sparse compute savings translate into real training speed.
key_works: Dai et al., 2024, *DeepSeekMoE*, arXiv:2401.06066; DeepSeek-AI, 2024, *DeepSeek-V3 Technical Report*, arXiv:2412.19437.

title: Optimal long-context activation storage
open: Jointly optimize recomputation, offloading, compression, and sequence parallelism for long-context training. Derive policies that adapt to memory hierarchy and bandwidth rather than using fixed heuristics.
status: FlashAttention and ZeRO reduce important memory costs. Complete activation-management optimization remains architecture- and hardware-dependent.
why: Enables longer contexts without disproportionate training cost.
key_works: Dao et al., 2022, *FlashAttention*, arXiv:2205.14135; Rajbhandari et al., 2019/2020, *ZeRO*, arXiv:1910.02054.

title: Efficient coupled rollout and training systems
open: Schedule generation, verification, reward computation, and parameter updates to maximize useful learning throughput. Control policy staleness, variable trajectory length, and verifier bottlenecks.
status: Reasoning RL and test-time scaling make rollout generation central to capability improvement. Joint systems optimization differs from optimizing training or serving in isolation.
why: Reduces the cost of post-training on interactive and verifiable tasks.
key_works: DeepSeek-AI, 2025, *DeepSeek-R1*, arXiv:2501.12948; Snell et al., 2024, *Scaling LLM Test-Time Compute Optimally*, arXiv:2408.03314.

title: KV-cache compression with task-level risk bounds
open: Compress or evict attention-cache state while bounding degradation on specified task classes, especially rare dependencies and multi-step reasoning. Detect when a compressed history must be reconstructed.
status: PagedAttention improves cache allocation, and efficient-attention research reduces memory traffic. Semantic risk from cache approximation is a separate target.
why: Reduces serving memory without hidden long-context failures.
key_works: Kwon et al., 2023, *Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention*, arXiv:2309.06180; Dao, 2023, *FlashAttention-2*, arXiv:2307.08691.

title: Quantization that preserves rare capabilities
open: Quantize models while preserving uncommon languages, numerical behavior, calibration, and safety-critical edge cases. Optimize worst-group or tail performance rather than only average benchmark loss.
status: GPTQ and AWQ demonstrate strong post-training quantization methods from 2022–2023. Their existence does not establish preservation of every rare capability.
why: Makes compression safer for heterogeneous real users.
key_works: Frantar et al., 2022, *GPTQ*, arXiv:2210.17323; Lin et al., 2023, *AWQ*, arXiv:2306.00978.

title: Disaggregated serving with predictable service levels
open: Coordinate prefill, decoding, cache transfer, and admission control to meet latency and availability targets under bursty mixed workloads. Include failure and overload behavior.
status: Splitwise and DistServe demonstrate benefits from separating serving phases. Stable service guarantees across demand distributions remain a broader operational target.
why: Improves utilization without sacrificing user-visible responsiveness.
key_works: Patel et al., 2023, *Splitwise*, arXiv:2311.18677; Zhong et al., 2024, *DistServe*, arXiv:2401.09670.

title: Speculative decoding that adapts optimally
open: Choose draft models, speculation lengths, and verification strategies online across changing requests and hardware. Preserve the required output distribution while accounting for communication and batching.
status: Exact speculative decoding is already established; it is not the open component. The target is broadly effective adaptive control under real serving conditions.
why: Converts theoretical token-generation savings into reliable application speedups.
key_works: Leviathan, Kalman, and Matias, 2022/2023, *Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding*, arXiv:2211.17192.

title: Shared inference caches without tenant leakage
open: Reuse prefixes, embeddings, and model state across requests without exposing another tenant’s data or access patterns. Define isolation rules that survive cache timing and eviction effects.
status: PagedAttention demonstrates efficient shared serving memory management. Privacy-safe cross-tenant reuse adds security requirements beyond allocation efficiency.
why: Retains caching benefits in sensitive multi-tenant deployments.
key_works: Kwon et al., 2023, *Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention*, arXiv:2309.06180; Knott et al., 2021, *CrypTen*, arXiv:2109.00984.

title: Fast cold starts without permanent idle capacity
open: Start models and agent environments quickly from cold storage while preserving reproducibility and isolation. Reduce initialization, weight-loading, compilation, and cache-building costs without keeping everything warm.
status: A June 2026 vLLM study directly analyzes cold-start latency. General low-cost startup across model sizes and hardware remains a concrete systems target.
why: Makes sparse demand and on-demand deployment economically viable.
key_works: Kabakibo, Trivedi, and Wang, 2026, *Breaking the Ice: Analyzing Cold Start Latency in vLLM*, arXiv:2606.07362.

title: Tenfold interactive inference improvement at fixed quality
open: Achieve at least a tenfold improvement in a preregistered combination of latency and cost per successful task on fixed hardware, without reducing task quality or concealing extra model calls.
status: FlashAttention, speculative decoding, and phase-disaggregated serving supply substantial ingredients. The proposed target requires end-to-end, workload-normalized validation.
why: Broadens applications that can afford responsive reasoning.
key_works: Dao, 2023, *FlashAttention-2*, arXiv:2307.08691; Leviathan et al., 2022/2023, *Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding*, arXiv:2211.17192; Zhong et al., 2024, *DistServe*, arXiv:2401.09670.

title: Hundredfold lower-energy useful edge assistance
open: Deliver a defined portfolio of offline assistant tasks at one-hundredth the energy of a declared baseline, including sensing, memory, and output. Preserve privacy, latency, and minimum capability requirements.
status: Quantization and byte-adaptive architectures offer partial efficiency gains. This is an explicit system-level moonshot, not a claim that a universal hundredfold gap is already measured.
why: Enables persistent assistance on phones, wearables, and embedded devices.
key_works: Lin et al., 2023, *AWQ*, arXiv:2306.00978; Pagnoni et al., 2024, *Byte Latent Transformer*, arXiv:2412.09871; Luccioni et al., 2023/2024, *Power Hungry Processing*, arXiv:2311.16863.

title: Analog inference robust to device drift
open: Maintain model quality as analog devices vary, age, heat, and drift, without calibration costs erasing their energy advantage. Include conversion, control, and memory overhead.
status: A 2023 analog-AI chip demonstrated speech-recognition and transcription workloads. Chip-level efficiency does not establish stable whole-system LLM deployment.
why: Could make analog acceleration practical rather than laboratory-specific.
key_works: Ambrogio et al., 2023, *An analog-AI chip for energy-efficient speech recognition and transcription*, DOI:10.1038/s41586-023-06337-5.

title: Photonic AI with favorable whole-system economics
open: Demonstrate end-to-end photonic acceleration whose advantages survive data conversion, nonlinear operations, memory movement, calibration, and manufacturing variation.
status: Coherent nanophotonic neural computation was demonstrated in 2016–2017. A useful optical matrix operation is only one component of a complete language-model system.
why: Tests whether photonics can materially improve practical AI efficiency.
key_works: Shen et al., 2016/2017, *Deep Learning with Coherent Nanophotonic Circuits*, arXiv:1610.02365; DOI:10.1038/nphoton.2017.93.

title: Neuromorphic systems for competitive language workloads
open: Develop learning and execution methods that exploit event-driven hardware on meaningful language and agent tasks, rather than merely mapping dense networks onto an ill-suited substrate.
status: Neuromorphic-computing research provides a broad physical and architectural foundation. Competitive language-task evaluation with full energy accounting remains a distinct target.
why: Explores alternatives to dense synchronous computation.
key_works: Marković et al., 2020, *Physics for Neuromorphic Computing*, arXiv:2003.04711; DOI:10.1038/s42254-020-0208-2.

title: Fundamental memory-movement limits for AI workloads
open: Characterize minimum data movement and energy for specified model computations across realistic memory hierarchies. Identify when near-memory or in-memory computing changes the achievable frontier.
status: I/O-aware attention methods establish important local results. Complete workloads include weights, activations, caches, routing, and conversion costs.
why: Distinguishes fundamental bottlenecks from implementation inefficiency.
key_works: Dao et al., 2022, *FlashAttention*, arXiv:2205.14135; Ambrogio et al., 2023, *An analog-AI chip*, DOI:10.1038/s41586-023-06337-5.

title: Low-energy interconnects for distributed AI
open: Reduce energy per useful distributed-training or inference operation by co-designing topology, communication algorithms, compression, and model partitioning. Include utilization and congestion effects.
status: DiLoCo reduces communication frequency, while automated parallelization optimizes placement. Network energy and model quality must still be optimized jointly.
why: Prevents communication from consuming the savings of faster arithmetic.
key_works: Douillard et al., 2023, *DiLoCo*, arXiv:2311.08105; Zheng et al., 2022, *Alpa*, arXiv:2201.12023.

title: Joint water–carbon–latency optimization
open: Schedule AI workloads while accounting for local water stress, electricity carbon intensity, latency, and cooling constraints. Avoid reducing one footprint by exporting harm to another resource or region.
status: Carbon and water studies establish relevant accounting approaches, often with substantial estimation uncertainty. Joint operational optimization requires better local measurements.
why: Makes environmental optimization multidimensional rather than cosmetic.
key_works: Patterson et al., 2021, *Carbon Emissions and Large Neural Network Training*, arXiv:2104.10350; Li et al., 2023, *Making AI Less “Thirsty”*, arXiv:2304.03271.

title: Auditable lifecycle footprints for AI services
open: Measure embodied hardware impacts, training, inference, replacement cycles, and shared-infrastructure allocation using auditable functional units and uncertainty ranges.
status: Chasing Carbon and Power Hungry Processing address important lifecycle and deployment components. Provider-comparable full-service accounting remains incomplete.
why: Enables credible environmental comparisons and procurement decisions.
key_works: Gupta et al., 2020/2021, *Chasing Carbon*, arXiv:2011.02839; Luccioni et al., 2023/2024, *Power Hungry Processing*, arXiv:2311.16863.

title: Carbon-aware scheduling without rebound or hidden trade-offs
open: Shift flexible computation to cleaner times and places while accounting for marginal rather than average emissions, data movement, capacity expansion, and induced additional demand.
status: Carbon-aware training analyses provide a foundation. Net system-wide benefit requires more than choosing a region with a favorable annual average.
why: Determines whether scheduling interventions reduce actual emissions.
key_works: Patterson et al., 2021, *Carbon Emissions and Large Neural Network Training*, arXiv:2104.10350; Gupta et al., 2020/2021, *Chasing Carbon*, arXiv:2011.02839.

title: Eliminating unsupported visual claims
open: Make visual-language systems distinguish observed objects and attributes from plausible but unobserved ones. Evaluate small, occluded, unusual, and contextually unexpected content.
status: POPE introduced targeted object-hallucination evaluation in 2023. Object presence is only one part of grounded visual description.
why: Improves assistive vision, inspection, and document understanding.
key_works: Li et al., 2023, *Evaluating Object Hallucination in Large Vision-Language Models*, arXiv:2305.10355.

title: Reliable visual attribute and relation binding
open: Correctly bind attributes, actions, and relations to the right entities in crowded or compositionally novel scenes. Resist language-only shortcuts.
status: Winoground and SugarCrepe provide concrete compositional evaluations from 2022–2023. Strong aggregate vision-language scores do not imply robust binding.
why: Supports precise visual reasoning rather than bag-of-concepts recognition.
key_works: Thrush et al., 2022, *Winoground*, arXiv:2204.03162; Hsieh et al., 2023, *SugarCrepe*, arXiv:2306.14610.

title: Metric geometry from multimodal observations
open: Infer distances, scale, orientation, and spatial uncertainty well enough to support actions, while identifying ambiguities that cannot be resolved from the available views.
status: Vision-language and robot models provide useful representations and action transfer. Reliable metric reconstruction with explicit uncertainty is a stronger requirement.
why: Connects descriptive perception to manipulation, navigation, and measurement.
key_works: Brohan et al., 2023, *RT-2*, arXiv:2307.15818; Open X-Embodiment Collaboration, 2023, *Open X-Embodiment*, arXiv:2310.08864.

title: Causal understanding of video
open: Distinguish temporal coincidence from causal interaction in video and predict consequences of interventions. Evaluate counterfactual changes rather than only event labels.
status: Video-MME evaluates broad video understanding, and Genie demonstrates interactive generative environments. Causal fidelity is not implied by visually plausible prediction.
why: Supports physical reasoning and trustworthy simulation.
key_works: Fu et al., 2024, *Video-MME*, arXiv:2405.21075; Bruce et al., 2024, *Genie: Generative Interactive Environments*, arXiv:2402.15391.

title: Rare-event detection in very long video
open: Detect brief, consequential events in hours or days of video without processing every frame at maximum cost. Quantify missed-event risk and temporal localization accuracy.
status: Long-video evaluation has progressed through benchmarks such as Video-MME. Rare-event guarantees and streaming resource constraints require additional datasets and methods.
why: Enables monitoring, scientific observation, and accessibility at realistic scale.
key_works: Fu et al., 2024, *Video-MME*, arXiv:2405.21075; Liu et al., 2023, *Lost in the Middle*, arXiv:2307.03172.

title: Full-duplex speech with reliable turn and intent management
open: Handle interruption, overlap, hesitation, background speakers, and corrections without losing intent or taking unintended actions. Evaluate latency and semantic accuracy jointly.
status: Moshi demonstrated real-time speech-text dialogue in 2024. Natural timing and safe action interpretation across diverse acoustic conditions remain wider targets.
why: Makes voice agents usable outside clean turn-taking demonstrations.
key_works: Défossez et al., 2024, *Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue*, arXiv:2410.00037.

title: Robust provenance for transformed synthetic media
open: Attribute or authenticate generated media after compression, editing, paraphrasing, and cross-modal transformation, with low false accusations and explicit limits against determined attackers.
status: Watermarking methods and detection-limit analyses exist. Universal reliable detection from content alone is not an appropriate unqualified target.
why: Supports trustworthy provenance without overstating forensic certainty.
key_works: Kirchenbauer et al., 2023, *A Watermark for Large Language Models*, arXiv:2301.10226; Sadasivan et al., 2023, *Can AI-Generated Text be Reliably Detected?*, arXiv:2303.11156.

title: World models that remain physically useful under intervention
open: Learn generative environments whose responses to actions preserve relevant physical constraints and predict real outcomes outside demonstrated trajectories. Evaluate control usefulness, not only visual realism.
status: Genie provides a concrete 2024 interactive world-model example; robotics transfer research supplies external validation settings.
why: Makes learned simulation useful for planning, training, and scientific reasoning.
key_works: Bruce et al., 2024, *Genie*, arXiv:2402.15391; Tobin et al., 2017, *Domain Randomization for Transferring Deep Neural Networks from Simulation to the Real World*, arXiv:1703.06907.

title: Transfer to genuinely new robot embodiments
open: Transfer skills to robots with different kinematics, sensors, grippers, and action spaces using minimal new data. Separate embodiment transfer from retraining on a closely related platform.
status: Open X-Embodiment and Octo demonstrate cross-robot data and generalist policies. Broad, low-data transfer to unseen embodiments remains a stronger goal.
why: Avoids rebuilding the learning stack for every robot.
key_works: Open X-Embodiment Collaboration, 2023, *Open X-Embodiment*, arXiv:2310.08864; Octo Model Team, 2024, *Octo*, arXiv:2405.12213.

title: Sim-to-real transfer under unknown dynamics
open: Transfer policies despite unmodeled friction, latency, compliance, wear, and contact behavior. Detect when simulation uncertainty is too large for safe deployment.
status: Domain randomization has been influential since 2017. Robust transfer across dynamics not captured by the randomization distribution remains unresolved.
why: Reduces expensive and risky real-world training.
key_works: Tobin et al., 2017, *Domain Randomization*, arXiv:1703.06907; Brunke et al., 2021/2022, *Safe Learning in Robotics*, arXiv:2108.06266.

title: General manipulation of deformable and contact-rich objects
open: Manipulate cloth, cables, bags, soft packaging, and irregular objects across unseen materials and arrangements. Recover from partial grasps, tangles, and uncertain contact.
status: Diffusion Policy and π0 demonstrate important manipulation capabilities, including selected deformable-object tasks. General robust handling remains broader than these demonstrations.
why: Unlocks practical household, warehouse, and manufacturing automation.
key_works: Chi et al., 2023, *Diffusion Policy*, arXiv:2303.04137; Black et al., 2024/2025, *π0: A Vision-Language-Action Flow Model for General Robot Control*, arXiv:2410.24164.

title: Tactile–visual dexterity that generalizes
open: Fuse touch and vision to control force, slip, and in-hand manipulation across objects and sensor layouts. Demonstrate transfer beyond a fixed tactile device and object set.
status: Generalist robot-policy research supplies scalable learning foundations. High-bandwidth contact feedback and sensor-transfer requirements make dexterity a distinct target.
why: Enables delicate and reliable manipulation beyond simple pick-and-place.
key_works: Octo Model Team, 2024, *Octo*, arXiv:2405.12213; Chi et al., 2023, *Diffusion Policy*, arXiv:2303.04137.

title: Learning robot skills from ordinary human demonstrations
open: Convert unconstrained human video into executable robot skills despite differences in embodiment, viewpoint, and missing force information. Quantify what additional interaction data is necessary.
status: RT-2 transfers web knowledge to robotic control, and Open X-Embodiment aggregates robot demonstrations. Neither makes arbitrary human video an immediately executable policy.
why: Greatly expands the pool of useful robot-training information.
key_works: Brohan et al., 2023, *RT-2*, arXiv:2307.15818; Open X-Embodiment Collaboration, 2023, *Open X-Embodiment*, arXiv:2310.08864.

title: Long-horizon embodied recovery
open: Complete multi-stage physical tasks while detecting and recovering from dropped objects, changed layouts, blocked paths, and depleted resources. Preserve safety throughout recovery.
status: Generalist robot models demonstrate increasingly diverse tasks. Sustained autonomy with robust recovery is a separate acceptance criterion.
why: Determines whether robots can work without frequent rescue.
key_works: Black et al., 2024/2025, *π0*, arXiv:2410.24164; Brunke et al., 2021/2022, *Safe Learning in Robotics*, arXiv:2108.06266.

title: Safety guarantees with learned robot dynamics
open: Provide useful safety guarantees when perception and dynamics models are learned and imperfect. Detect assumption violations quickly enough to switch to a safe fallback.
status: Safe-learning robotics research provides control-theoretic methods and an explicit open agenda. High-dimensional perception and unknown environments complicate certification.
why: Makes physical autonomy acceptable around people and valuable equipment.
key_works: Brunke et al., 2021/2022, *Safe Learning in Robotics: From Learning-Based Control to Safe Reinforcement Learning*, arXiv:2108.06266.

title: Hundredfold reduction in real robot experience
open: Match a declared multi-task robot baseline using at most one-hundredth as many real-world interaction episodes, with all simulation, demonstration, and teacher information accounted for.
status: Cross-embodiment datasets, generalist policies, and simulation transfer offer complementary approaches. The information-accounted hundredfold target is a proposed moonshot.
why: Could make robot development feasible outside a few well-funded laboratories.
key_works: Open X-Embodiment Collaboration, 2023, *Open X-Embodiment*, arXiv:2310.08864; Octo Model Team, 2024, *Octo*, arXiv:2405.12213; Tobin et al., 2017, *Domain Randomization*, arXiv:1703.06907.

title: Causally informative autonomous experiment selection
subfield: AI for science, mathematics, and discovery
open: Select experiments that discriminate among competing explanations rather than merely maximize a predicted property. Account for cost, feasibility, negative results, and model misspecification.
status: AI Scientist and Co-Scientist demonstrate automated research workflows. Causal experimental design with real-world validation remains a distinct scientific target.
why: Makes automated research produce knowledge rather than plausible reports.
key_works: Lu et al., 2024, *The AI Scientist*, arXiv:2408.06292; Gottweis et al., 2025, *Accelerating scientific discovery with Co-Scientist*, arXiv:2502.18864.

title: Certified neural surrogates for physical equations
subfield: AI for science, mathematics, and discovery
open: Produce fast learned PDE or simulation surrogates with useful error estimates, conservation properties, and stability guarantees outside training conditions. Detect when a conventional solver is required.
status: Physics-informed machine learning provides a broad 2021 framework. Small residuals or good interpolation do not automatically certify the physical solution.
why: Makes fast surrogates usable in consequential engineering and scientific calculations.
key_works: Karniadakis et al., 2021, *Physics-informed machine learning*, DOI:10.1038/s42254-021-00314-5.

title: Materials discovery that closes the synthesis loop
subfield: AI for science, mathematics, and discovery
open: Propose materials that can actually be synthesized, characterized, and reproduced with the desired properties. Include kinetics, defects, processing conditions, and failed synthesis attempts.
status: GNoME demonstrated large-scale computational materials discovery in 2023. Predicted stability is not identical to practical synthesis or useful manufactured performance.
why: Converts candidate databases into usable materials.
key_works: Merchant et al., 2023, *Scaling deep learning for materials discovery*, DOI:10.1038/s41586-023-06735-9.

title: Mechanism identification rather than predictive correlation
subfield: AI for science, mathematics, and discovery
open: Infer scientific mechanisms that survive intervention and competing-model tests, while representing nonidentifiability. Avoid treating a high-performing predictor as a mechanistic explanation.
status: Causal representation learning and AI research agents offer complementary ingredients. Mechanistic validity requires evidence beyond predictive fit.
why: Supports scientific understanding and reliable extrapolation.
key_works: Schölkopf et al., 2021, *Towards Causal Representation Learning*, arXiv:2102.11107; Gottweis et al., 2025, *Accelerating scientific discovery with Co-Scientist*, arXiv:2502.18864.

title: Novel theorem discovery with verified significance
subfield: AI for science, mathematics, and discovery
open: Generate mathematically novel conjectures, constructions, or proofs that are correct and substantively useful, with novelty checked against prior literature and significance assessed beyond trivial variations.
status: FunSearch produced new mathematical constructions, while LeanDojo supports formal proof search. Broad autonomous discovery and significance assessment remain larger targets.
why: Expands the frontier of machine-assisted mathematics.
key_works: Romera-Paredes et al., 2023/2024, *Mathematical discoveries from program search with large language models*, DOI:10.1038/s41586-023-06924-6; Yang et al., 2023, *LeanDojo*, arXiv:2306.15626.

title: Identifying scientific laws from noisy, partial observations
subfield: AI for science, mathematics, and discovery
open: Recover compact governing relationships from noisy data with hidden variables, measurement bias, and limited interventions. Distinguish multiple observationally equivalent laws.
status: Physics-informed learning and causal-representation research provide relevant constraints and frameworks. General law discovery under realistic nonidentifiability remains unresolved.
why: Could accelerate discovery while exposing what the data cannot determine.
key_works: Karniadakis et al., 2021, *Physics-informed machine learning*, DOI:10.1038/s42254-021-00314-5; Schölkopf et al., 2021, *Towards Causal Representation Learning*, arXiv:2102.11107.

title: Predicting biomolecular conformational ensembles and kinetics
subfield: AI for science, mathematics, and discovery
open: Predict distributions of biologically relevant conformations, transition rates, and condition-dependent interactions, with calibrated uncertainty and experimental validation.
status: AlphaFold 3 advanced biomolecular interaction structure prediction in 2024. Accurate structures do not by themselves determine complete dynamical ensembles or kinetics.
why: Supports mechanistic biology and more reliable molecular design.
key_works: Abramson et al., 2024, *Accurate structure prediction of biomolecular interactions with AlphaFold 3*, DOI:10.1038/s41586-024-07487-w.

title: Reproducible autonomous science with negative-result accounting
subfield: AI for science, mathematics, and discovery
open: Produce research workflows whose data, code, hypotheses, analysis decisions, and failed attempts can be independently reconstructed. Prevent selective reporting by automated systems.
status: AI Scientist and Co-Scientist demonstrate automation of research activities. Reproducibility and complete accounting of unsuccessful branches require explicit infrastructure and incentives.
why: Keeps accelerated research from accelerating irreproducibility.
key_works: Lu et al., 2024, *The AI Scientist*, arXiv:2408.06292; Gottweis et al., 2025, *Accelerating scientific discovery with Co-Scientist*, arXiv:2502.18864.

title: Resolving graph over-squashing without destructive rewiring
subfield: Structured-data learning and other AI paradigms
open: Preserve long-range graph information while maintaining relevant topology, locality, and computational efficiency. Identify when rewiring improves communication but changes the task’s meaning.
status: Over-squashing was explicitly analyzed in 2020–2021. Eliminating bottlenecks across arbitrary graph families without other losses remains open.
why: Improves reasoning on molecules, infrastructure, knowledge graphs, and relational systems.
key_works: Alon and Yahav, 2020/2021, *On the Bottleneck of Graph Neural Networks and its Practical Implications*, arXiv:2006.05205.

title: Scalable graph expressivity beyond message-passing limits
subfield: Structured-data learning and other AI paradigms
open: Increase graph-model distinguishability while retaining practical scaling and generalization. Characterize the useful expressivity–cost frontier rather than asking whether standard message passing has known limits.
status: Xu et al. established important expressivity relationships in 2018–2019. Those solved characterizations motivate, but do not solve, efficient richer architectures.
why: Enables models to represent relational distinctions that simpler architectures collapse.
key_works: Xu et al., 2018/2019, *How Powerful are Graph Neural Networks?*, arXiv:1810.00826.

title: Tabular foundation models under schema and causal shift
subfield: Structured-data learning and other AI paradigms
open: Transfer tabular learning across changing feature meanings, missingness mechanisms, sample sizes, and causal structures. Detect when the pretrained prior is inappropriate.
status: TabPFN demonstrated powerful prior-data fitting for small tabular classification in 2022–2023. The target here is robust transfer beyond a model’s supported prior regime.
why: Extends foundation-model benefits to common business and scientific datasets.
key_works: Hollmann et al., 2022/2023, *TabPFN: A Transformer That Solves Small Tabular Classification Problems in a Second*, arXiv:2207.01848.

title: Time-series foundation models under structural breaks
subfield: Structured-data learning and other AI paradigms
open: Forecast and quantify uncertainty through regime changes, interventions, irregular sampling, and changing seasonal structure. Distinguish predictable recurrence from genuinely new dynamics.
status: Chronos demonstrated language-model-style time-series learning in 2024. Robustness to structural breaks requires more than strong average forecasting benchmarks.
why: Supports reliable forecasting in finance, energy, logistics, and science.
key_works: Ansari et al., 2024, *Chronos: Learning the Language of Time Series*, arXiv:2403.07815.

title: Recommender learning without self-induced confounding
subfield: Structured-data learning and other AI paradigms
open: Learn user benefit from data generated by prior recommendations without mistaking exposure effects for preferences. Evaluate long-term welfare, diversity, and feedback dynamics.
status: Chaney et al. demonstrated recommendation feedback-loop confounding in simulations in 2017–2018. Eliminating it in deployed adaptive systems remains a larger target.
why: Prevents systems from manufacturing the behavior they later claim to predict.
key_works: Chaney, Stewart, and Engelhardt, 2017/2018, *How Algorithmic Confounding in Recommendation Systems Increases Homogeneity and Decreases Utility*, arXiv:1710.11214.

title: Safe test-time adaptation without labels
subfield: Structured-data learning and other AI paradigms
open: Adapt to deployment shifts using unlabeled observations while detecting when adaptation would reinforce errors or respond to adversarial data. Bound damage and support rollback.
status: Tent demonstrated entropy-minimization adaptation in 2020–2021. Lower predictive entropy is not a universal signal of improved correctness.
why: Enables adaptation without uncontrolled deployment-time drift.
key_works: Wang et al., 2020/2021, *Tent: Fully Test-time Adaptation by Entropy Minimization*, arXiv:2006.10726.

title: Weakly supervised disentanglement with useful guarantees
subfield: Structured-data learning and other AI paradigms
open: Determine which minimal labels, interventions, temporal assumptions, or structural priors make latent factors identifiable and useful. Do not ask for unrestricted unsupervised identifiability already ruled out in known settings.
status: Locatello et al. established important impossibility and empirical results in 2018–2019. The remaining target concerns sufficient weak supervision and practical recovery.
why: Supports controllable representations and causal transfer.
key_works: Locatello et al., 2018/2019, *Challenging Common Assumptions in the Unsupervised Learning of Disentangled Representations*, arXiv:1811.12359; Schölkopf et al., 2021, *Towards Causal Representation Learning*, arXiv:2102.11107.

title: Discovering meaningful new classes in open worlds
subfield: Structured-data learning and other AI paradigms
open: Detect unfamiliar entities and organize them into useful new categories without confusing sensor noise, distribution shift, and genuine novelty. Support incremental labeling and revision.
status: OpenMax provides an established open-set rejection method. Discovering stable new semantic categories is a stronger task than rejecting unknown inputs.
why: Lets AI systems expand their concepts after deployment.
key_works: Bendale and Boult, 2015/2016, *Towards Open Set Deep Networks*, arXiv:1511.06233.

title: Offline RL beyond observed action coverage
subfield: Reinforcement learning, continual learning, and open-ended adaptation
open: Learn useful policies from logged data while explicitly identifying where unsupported actions make value estimates unreliable. Characterize when additional assumptions or experiments permit safe extrapolation.
status: Offline RL has a mature problem formulation and extensive methods, summarized in 2020. General reliable extrapolation beyond coverage is not supplied by pessimism alone.
why: Enables learning from existing operational data without dangerous trial-and-error.
key_works: Levine et al., 2020, *Offline Reinforcement Learning: Tutorial, Review, and Perspectives on Open Problems*, arXiv:2005.01643.

title: Efficient exploration with extremely sparse rewards
subfield: Reinforcement learning, continual learning, and open-ended adaptation
open: Discover useful behaviors when success is rare and naive exploration is too expensive or unsafe. Avoid intrinsic objectives that produce novelty unrelated to eventual goals.
status: Unsupervised skill-discovery methods such as DIAYN provide reusable behaviors. Connecting discovered diversity to difficult downstream tasks remains open.
why: Reduces dependence on dense reward engineering.
key_works: Eysenbach et al., 2018/2019, *Diversity is All You Need: Learning Skills without a Reward Function*, arXiv:1802.06070.

title: Safe transition from offline learning to online improvement
subfield: Reinforcement learning, continual learning, and open-ended adaptation
open: Improve a policy online after offline initialization while controlling risk from distribution shift and uncertain value estimates. Specify when exploration is justified and when it must stop.
status: Offline RL and safe-robotics research supply separate tools. Their combination in high-dimensional, partially observed settings remains demanding.
why: Allows systems to improve after deployment without discarding safety constraints.
key_works: Levine et al., 2020, *Offline Reinforcement Learning*, arXiv:2005.01643; Brunke et al., 2021/2022, *Safe Learning in Robotics*, arXiv:2108.06266.

title: Generalization across procedurally generated environments
subfield: Reinforcement learning, continual learning, and open-ended adaptation
open: Learn policies that transfer to new environment structures rather than memorizing superficial variation. Construct procedural distributions that expose genuine strategy transfer.
status: CoinRun quantified generalization challenges in 2018–2019. Generalizing within one generator does not establish transfer to different mechanics or causal structure.
why: Improves the validity of reinforcement-learning progress measurements.
key_works: Cobbe et al., 2018/2019, *Quantifying Generalization in Reinforcement Learning*, arXiv:1812.02341.

title: Continual learning without unbounded replay
subfield: Reinforcement learning, continual learning, and open-ended adaptation
open: Learn an evolving stream of tasks while preserving useful prior capabilities under bounded memory and compute. Measure both forgetting and the ability to revise obsolete knowledge.
status: Elastic weight consolidation addressed catastrophic forgetting in 2016–2017. General stability–plasticity trade-offs remain unresolved, especially under unknown task boundaries.
why: Enables models that improve continuously without repeated full retraining.
key_works: Kirkpatrick et al., 2016/2017, *Overcoming catastrophic forgetting in neural networks*, arXiv:1612.00796.

title: Predictable model merging
subfield: Reinforcement learning, continual learning, and open-ended adaptation
open: Combine independently trained capabilities while predicting interference, preserving constraints, and avoiding exhaustive evaluation of every mixture. Include models with different training histories.
status: Model soups demonstrated useful weight averaging in 2022. Arbitrary capability composition and safety preservation are stronger requirements.
why: Could make model development modular and reduce repeated training.
key_works: Wortsman et al., 2022, *Model soups: averaging weights of multiple fine-tuned models improves accuracy without increasing inference time*, arXiv:2203.05482.

title: Off-policy evaluation with hidden confounding
subfield: Reinforcement learning, continual learning, and open-ended adaptation
open: Estimate a new policy’s consequences from observational logs when action selection depends on unrecorded information. Return valid uncertainty or partial-identification bounds when point estimates are unjustified.
status: Offline RL formalizes evaluation from logged experience; real operational data can violate the assumptions needed for ordinary estimators.
why: Prevents unsafe policy deployment based on biased retrospective estimates.
key_works: Levine et al., 2020, *Offline Reinforcement Learning*, arXiv:2005.01643; Chaney et al., 2017/2018, *How Algorithmic Confounding in Recommendation Systems Increases Homogeneity and Decreases Utility*, arXiv:1710.11214.

title: Open-ended skill accumulation without aimless novelty
subfield: Reinforcement learning, continual learning, and open-ended adaptation
open: Accumulate increasingly useful skills without a fixed final task while avoiding redundancy, trivial novelty, and destructive interference. Define measurable progress that cannot be cheaply gamed.
status: DIAYN demonstrates reward-free skill diversity, and intelligence-measurement work emphasizes learning new skills. Sustained useful open-endedness is a broader target.
why: Supports agents that become more capable through experience.
key_works: Eysenbach et al., 2018/2019, *Diversity is All You Need*, arXiv:1802.06070; Chollet, 2019, *On the Measure of Intelligence*, arXiv:1911.01547.

title: Demonstrating net clinical benefit prospectively
open: Show that an AI-assisted clinical workflow improves patient-relevant outcomes under real staffing, incentives, and case mix, without unacceptable subgroup harms or additional diagnostic error.
status: Medical-language benchmarks and clinical decision-making evaluations establish capability and limitations. Benchmark performance is not a substitute for prospective outcome evidence.
why: Determines whether clinical deployment actually helps patients.
key_works: Singhal et al., 2022/2023, *Large Language Models Encode Clinical Knowledge*, arXiv:2212.13138; Hager et al., 2024, *Evaluation and mitigation of the limitations of large language models in clinical decision-making*, DOI:10.1038/s41591-024-03097-1.

title: Legal reasoning under jurisdiction and temporal change
open: Produce legally relevant analysis that tracks jurisdiction, controlling authority, procedural posture, and the law applicable at the relevant date. Detect when an apparently analogous case is not controlling.
status: LegalBench introduced 162 tasks across six legal-reasoning types in 2023. Reliable, continuously updated professional workflows are a larger target.
why: Reduces confident legal analysis based on the wrong authority or time period.
key_works: Guha et al., 2023, *LegalBench: A Collaboratively Built Benchmark for Measuring Legal Reasoning in Large Language Models*, arXiv:2308.11462.

title: Contestable AI-assisted public decisions
open: Design systems in which affected people can understand, challenge, and correct consequential AI-assisted decisions without needing model expertise or access to proprietary internals.
status: Model cards and verifiable-claim frameworks improve documentation. Effective contestability requires procedures, evidence access, and remedies beyond disclosure.
why: Preserves accountability and due process.
key_works: Mitchell et al., 2018/2019, *Model Cards for Model Reporting*, arXiv:1810.03993; Brundage et al., 2020, *Toward Trustworthy AI Development*, arXiv:2004.07213.

title: Correlated financial risk from shared AI models
open: Measure whether widespread use of similar models creates synchronized decisions, liquidity shocks, or hidden concentration of operational risk. Distinguish ordinary correlation from model-induced feedback.
status: Foundation-model concentration and cooperative-agent research motivate the concern. Credible measurement requires financial-system data and explicit counterfactuals.
why: Identifies systemic risks that are invisible in single-firm evaluations.
key_works: Bommasani et al., 2021, *On the Opportunities and Risks of Foundation Models*, arXiv:2108.07258; Dafoe et al., 2020, *Open Problems in Cooperative AI*, arXiv:2012.08630.

title: Measuring AI incidents without denominator blindness
open: Estimate incident rates and severity with meaningful exposure denominators, consistent classifications, and reporting-bias correction. Avoid interpreting raw report counts as population risk.
status: The AI Incident Database established an important cataloging approach in 2020–2021. Catalogs alone do not identify incidence rates.
why: Makes safety trends and intervention effectiveness measurable.
key_works: McGregor, 2020/2021, *Preventing Repeated Real World AI Failures by Cataloging Incidents: The AI Incident Database*, arXiv:2011.08512.

title: Validating red-team results against field failures
open: Determine which red-team findings predict real incidents and which deployment failures current testing systematically misses. Measure both predictive value and coverage.
status: AgentDojo supplies structured adversarial evaluation, while incident databases record real events. Connecting the two requires prospective evidence.
why: Directs safety resources toward tests that actually reduce harm.
key_works: Debenedetti et al., 2024, *AgentDojo*, arXiv:2406.13352; McGregor, 2020/2021, *Preventing Repeated Real World AI Failures*, arXiv:2011.08512.

title: Causal attribution of responsibility in AI supply chains
open: Reconstruct which contributions from model developers, deployers, data providers, tool operators, and users caused a harmful outcome. Design evidence retention compatible with privacy and trade-secret constraints.
status: Provenance and verifiable-claim frameworks provide relevant documentation mechanisms. Responsibility in multi-party, adaptive systems requires additional causal and institutional analysis.
why: Supports effective remediation, insurance, and accountability.
key_works: Longpre et al., 2023, *The Data Provenance Initiative*, arXiv:2310.16787; Brundage et al., 2020, *Toward Trustworthy AI Development*, arXiv:2004.07213.

title: Discriminating tests for AI consciousness and welfare relevance
open: Develop empirically discriminating methods for evaluating theories of consciousness in artificial systems, while distinguishing verbal self-report, functional indicators, and moral uncertainty.
status: Butlin et al. synthesized theory-derived indicators in 2023. There is no implication that present systems are conscious, nor a settled test that resolves the question.
why: Informs cautious decisions about potentially welfare-relevant future systems.
key_works: Butlin et al., 2023, *Consciousness in Artificial Intelligence: Insights from the Science of Consciousness*, arXiv:2308.08708.

title: Independent access to frontier-relevant research compute
open: Establish sustained access that lets independent researchers reproduce important capability, safety, and systems experiments, including publication of unfavorable findings. Measure whether allocations match actual experimental needs.
status: Industry concentration has been documented, and the NSF’s NAIRR provides a concrete shared-resource initiative. The target is sufficient, durable, independently usable access—not the absence of all public programs.
why: Broadens who can verify claims and propose alternatives.
key_works: Ahmed, Wahed, and Thompson, 2023, *The growing influence of industry in AI research*, DOI:10.1126/science.ade2420; NSF, 2026, *National Artificial Intelligence Research Resource*.

title: Sustained funding for community language infrastructure
open: Fund ongoing corpus maintenance, evaluation, compensation, and local technical capacity rather than one-time data collection. Establish community control over priorities and downstream access.
status: Linguistic-resource inequality and provenance gaps are documented. Durable maintenance and benefit-sharing require institutional support beyond publishing a dataset.
why: Prevents low-resource language projects from disappearing after a grant ends.
